$schema_notes.purpose: PLAN-36 T00 critical-action registry: machine-readable inventory of authenticated ThemisIQ UI actions, driving both a static schema test (tests/test_ui_action_registry.py) and real-browser tests (tests/ui/). Validated by tests/test_ui_action_registry.py -- keep that file and this schema note in sync.
$schema_notes.coverage: This is a curated slice covering every action named in plans/PLAN-36-themisiq-stabilization-and-product-improvements/findings.md (F01-F08), plus the login/navigation actions T00's own completion gate requires. It intentionally does NOT yet enumerate all ~993 buttons/398 links/1341 onclick handlers the audit counted app-wide -- that full inventory is future incremental work (see oneforall/scripts/dev/scan_ui_actions.py, which drafts candidate entries from template source for a human to promote into this file). Each stabilization task (T01-T06) is expected to add/update the entries for the module it touches as it lands its own browser tests.

fields.id: stable dotted identifier, never reused for a different action
fields.route: GET page path that renders/hosts the control (not the mutation endpoint)
fields.label: visible text/name of the control
fields.required_capability: core.rbac capability string or role_key gating this action, or null if only login is required
fields.backend: {method, path} of the HTTP endpoint the action ultimately calls; for a pure client-side toggle (e.g. modal open) this is the GET route of the page that hosts it
fields.personas: role_key values (core/rbac.py) permitted to see/use this action, or ['anonymous'] pre-login
fields.fixture: prerequisite synthetic data/state needed before the action can be exercised
fields.expected_failure_ui: observable UI signal on failure; required for every mutation action
fields.notes: optional free text, e.g. a pointer to the findings.md defect this action currently exhibits

actions.label: Test
actions.fixture: one saved webhook pointed at a controlled local HTTP fixture the test owns (never a third party); validate_outbound_url's HTTPS/public-DNS check is monkeypatched for just that local fixture, the same way tests/test_webhook_test_endpoint.py does it

actions.expected_failure_ui: a genuine delivery failure (fixture returns 5xx/times out/blocked) surfaces as 'Failed' on the button, with a sanitized reason in its title attribute -- never the success state
actions.notes: FIXED by T05 (was FINDING F06 + F07, security release blocker). modules/launcher/routes_admin.py:api_webhook_test now calls core.webhooks.send_test_ping, a real single signed attempt through core/outbound_http.py (F07's shared HTTPS + public-DNS-only policy, revalidated immediately before connecting), rate-limited per actor+webhook. Covered by tests/test_webhook_test_endpoint.py (HTTP level: real delivery, truthful failure, org isolation, rate limit, blocked-destination) and tests/ui/test_webhook_admin_ui.py (browser: Sending/Delivered/Failed states, double-click suppression proven by asserting the fixture server receives exactly one request).

actions.label: + Add Template
actions.fixture: authenticated session with erm.library.manage (super_admin or risk_owner per core/rbac.py:232)
actions.expected_success_ui: an add/edit template modal becomes visible
actions.notes: FINDING F03 (high, currently red) + F13 (tenant-isolation blocker on the same button): modules/erm/templates/index.html:473 renders #libAdminBtn with style="display:none" permanently and its onclick calls the undefined ermOpenLibraryModal(). Per findings.md F13, erm_risk_library has no org_id/creator scope today, so simply un-hiding this button would let any risk_owner (not just platform super admins) mutate the global catalogue every organization reads. destructive_test_policy is manual_only until T03 lands org_id scoping and a can_manage_library gate -- do not automate create/update/delete against this endpoint before then.

actions.expected_success_ui: form fields reload to the last persisted server configuration; masked secrets stay masked
actions.expected_failure_ui: visible error state (403/500/network), not a silent no-op
actions.notes: FIXED by T03 (was FINDING F04, high): the button now calls window.resetConfig, not the unattached loadConfig -- covered by tests/ui/test_erm_library_and_email_reset.py::test_email_reset_reloads_without_error. T06 (findings.md F08) additionally migrated loadConfig's fetch onto ApiClient.request, so a load failure now throws a typed error with the server's real detail instead of a hand-rolled status-code message.
